ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, HM Treasury sanctions list, and the U.S. Treasury OFAC SDN List where any USD or cross-border transactions are anticipated; Cyprus obliged entities also apply domestic checks under Law 13(I)/2021 and FATF-criteria Enhanced Due Diligence for Politically Exposed Persons, including source-of-wealth verification and senior-management approval where required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR), electronic Company Name Reservation and e-Filing service (efiling.drcor.mcit.gov.cy)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Cyprus private limited company may be registered using a Greek- or English-script name. Latin-script names are transliterated into Greek characters for the official name register and may be used in English documentation without restriction; characters outside the Greek/Latin alphabets are inadmissible, and the proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved name. The name must end in 'Limited' or 'Ltd' for a private limited company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its registered agent may submit a written reconsideration request to DRCOR within 14 days of notification, proposing a corrected name and, if the ground is a sensitive token, attaching the relevant ministerial or supervisory consent. If the objection is denied, an annulment recourse may be filed with the Administrative Court under Article 146 of the Constitution of Cyprus within 75 days. A prior reservation may be extended for a further 180-day period by applying to DRCOR before expiry and evidencing active incorporation steps or pending ministerial approval.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or serviced office is permissible only if it constitutes a physical address in Cyprus at which legal process may be served and notices from the Registrar can be received during normal working hours; a mere P.O. Box will not satisfy the statutory registered-office requirement. For this low-risk e-commerce wooden toy trading company, a commercial registered-office service is acceptable, but it must be able to retain statutory records and official correspondence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a non-resident e-commerce holding/sales entity: approximately 5% annual likelihood of unannounced inspection at the registered office; the likelihood rises to 10-15% if Cyprus VAT registration, Cyprus tax residency, or a CySEC-regulated license is sought.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113 (as amended), Sections 4, 9, 18 and 20; Companies (Fees) Rules; Income Tax Law No. 118(I)/2002 for subsequent tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry) through the Ariadne integrated e-platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Company Registration Form HE1) together with the Declaration of Compliance (Form HE2) and Statement of Share Capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Company must issue at least one share. Standard Cyprus practice adopts a registered share capital of EUR 1,000 divided into 1,000 ordinary shares of EUR 1.00 each, with at least one share fully paid-up before filing; no escrow account is required by Cypriot law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, unanimously, that the Company adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Registrar; that the subscribers’ allotment of ordinary shares be approved and recorded in the Register of Members; that the registered office at [registered office address] be adopted as the statutory seat; and that [Director 1], [Director 2] be appointed Directors and [Corporate Secretary] be appointed Corporate Secretary. FURTHER RESOLVED that the Directors are authorised to open bank accounts, register for income tax, VAT and social insurance, and execute all documents necessary to effect these resolutions. ANY two Directors may sign on behalf of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name approval and constitutional document preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (online via Ariadne portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name-reservation application and receive a Name Approval Certificate. Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English or Greek, have subscribers’ signatures notarised or certified, and complete statutory Forms HE1 and HE2.
required_dossiers: Notarised Memorandum and Articles of Association
Passport copies and proof of residential address of each subscriber/director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or the Registry issues a query, file a written objection or alternative name request through the Ariadne portal within 14 days. Correct any defects in the constitutional documents and resubmit the amended forms without additional State fee when the query was purely formal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company incorporation filing, execution and certificate issue
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (Ariadne e-filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the official filing fee, upload the signed constitutional documents and statutory forms, and submit the incorporation application. The Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Number; then obtain certified copies of the constitution and register of directors.
required_dossiers: Notarised Memorandum and Articles of Association
Proof of payment of filing fee
Consent forms for Directors and Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns the application, pay the administrative cure fee where applicable, amend the filed document to the extent permitted, and re-submit within 30 days. For substantive rejections, a new incorporation package must be prepared.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Department and VAT Service of the Republic of Cyprus (TAXISnet)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days of incorporation, register the Company for income and defence tax and obtain a Cyprus Tax Identification Number (TIN). If taxable turnover exceeds EUR 15,600 per year or is projected to do so, submit the VAT registration form V1. Register the toy-manufacturing activity under ISIC 3240.
required_dossiers: Passports of directors and beneficial owners
Bank confirmation of issued capital if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File the V1/V2 form through TAXISnet as soon as omitted and request late-filing penalty waiver with a reasoned justification. If the tax authority contests the requested VAT date, appeal to the VAT Appeals Committee within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Social Insurance Services – Ministry of Labour and Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company as an employer on the Social Insurance register and obtain an Employer Number. Complete employee registration forms and set up monthly PAYE/defence deductions for all staff. Issue contract statements before commencement of works.
required_dossiers: Bank details for social fund payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the employer number is delayed, personally deliver the registration to the local Social Insurance office and obtain a receipt. Late registration penalties may be appealed via the Social Insurance Disciplinary Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial establishment licensing and planning approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Urban Development Office and Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry (Industrial Activities Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to manufacturing, submit an application for an industrial establishment licence and, if required, a change-of-use permit for the production premises. Include site plans, structural load data, fire safety layout, and waste handling scheme. Obtain approval from the District Officer for light-manufacturing activity.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership title of premises
Fire safety certificate from Fire Service
Environmental registration or preliminary EIA report (if triggered)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal adverse licencing decisions to the Minister of Energy, Commerce and Industry within 30 days. If the objection relates to planning, file a recourse to the Administrative Court. Correct the premises safety deficiencies and resubmit together with the improvement certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry – Industrial Activities Division; District Administration for permits; Town Planning and Housing Department for premises use consent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Establishment Licence for Light Manufacturing (Issued under the Control of Industrial Establishment and Works Laws, Cap. 59 as amended; Building use permit under Cap. 96).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment – Environmental Protection Agency, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (Registration / Preliminary Environmental Report) for the operation of small-scale beechwood toy turning and assembly units; full EIA Report is not required when the covered area is below 1,000 m2 and no solvent-based adhesives are used.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must comply with urban wastewater thresholds (COD ≤125 mg/L; BOD5 ≤25 mg/L; TSS ≤35 mg/L). VOC emissions from any varnishing/adhesive operations must not exceed 50 mg C/m3 and use of solvent-free formulations is mandatory. Wood dust filtration and capture equipment must maintain airborne dust below 3 mg/m3. Non-hazardous sawdust must be recycled or sent to an authorised composting facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Fire Department under the Fire Prevention and Civil Defense Law; structural load inspection certificate from the District Civil Defence for multi-storey premises; Occupational Health & Safety clearance from the Labor Inspection Department covering machine guarding for wood-cutting equipment, emergency exits, first-aid provisions and noise control below 87 dB(a).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax Department, Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Cyprus; web portal: https://taxportal.mof.gov.cy
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident entities must obtain a Cyprus Tax Identification Code (TIC) by submitting Form TD 2001 (Tax Registration Certificate Application) to the District Tax Office, along with certified M&A, Certificate of Incorporation, registered office address, and proof of identity of directors and ultimate beneficial owners. VAT registration is mandatory for non-resident suppliers of taxable goods/services, with registration completed through the same Tax Portal using Form VAT 101; a VAT registration number is issued within 10-20 business days if a fiscal representative is appointed when required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cyprus does not operate a check-the-box regime. Elections available include: notional interest deduction (NID) election on new equity, tax residence certification election (to confirm central management and control), optional VAT grouping (Form VAT 112), and election to continue old tax rules for amortization of goodwill and IP under transitional provisions. Hybrid mismatch rules under CySec Circular and Income Tax Law 118(I)2002 (art. 18AA) restrict elective treatment but no entity classification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax under Cyprus VAT Law 32(I)/2000, transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 15,600 annual taxable turnover for Cyprus-established entities; non-established taxable persons have no threshold and are compulsorily registerable from the first taxable supply. Distance sales of goods from other EU member states trigger registration at EUR 10,000 per calendar year.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Cyprus does not mandate continuous transaction controls, real-time fiscal clearance, or digital stamping. Mandatory electronic reporting of VAT returns and VIES periodic declarations via the Tax Portal is required; e-invoicing using PEPPOL is recommended but not compulsory. No real-time interface / API stamping is currently enforced, though the Tax Department has announced gradual transition to EU e-invoicing standards under ViDA.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (a) export of tangible goods physically departing Cyprus to a destination outside the EU, evidenced by customs declaration and transport documents; (b) supplies of services tied directly to exported goods (e.g., loading, packing) for goods exported within one year; (c) international transport and related services; and (d) intra-Community supplies of goods transferred to VAT-registered persons in other EU states subject to valid VAT number and listing in VIES. For baby montessori wooden blocks (ISIC 3240), zero-rating is available provided title in goods transfers to a non-resident buyer and goods leave Cyprus within 90 days of dispatch.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document AE0 / SAD)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by carrier confirming physical departure
Commercial invoice referencing contract terms and Incoterms
Inward Remittance Certificate showing receipt of export proceeds
Proof of VAT identity of overseas recipient (for intra-Community zero-rating)
Bank transfer / SWIFT confirmation of export invoice settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Tax Department may reverse zero-rating and charge 19% VAT where the 180-day FX repatriation deadline is missed without justified commercial cause or documentation is falsified. Penalties include interim assessment, 2% interest per month on unpaid VAT, surcharge of 10% on late payment, administrative penalty up to EUR 100 per non-listed transaction, and criminal liability for fraudulent evasion under VAT Law and Criminal Code, with fines up to EUR 40,000 or imprisonment of up to three years. Retrospective clawbacks also apply where goods are re-imported to Cyprus or documentation fails the 'inward timeline' test.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (CB Cyprus) acting as the national competent authority for monetary stability, banking supervision, and balance-of-payments reporting, in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) for euro area payment oversight and Eurosystem liquidity operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro (EUR) is fully convertible; Cyprus maintains no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions as an EU/EMU member. Non-resident shareholders may freely re-capitalize the Cyprus Ltd and repatriate dividends; profit remittance is not subject to withholding tax or Central Bank of Cyprus approval. The only administrative duty is statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the CB Cyprus for settlements equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Cyprus imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds. The exporter may retain receipts indefinitely in USD, EUR, or any other currency in domestic or foreign bank accounts. The statutory ECB/CB Cyprus reporting framework only requires transaction-level submission for goods exports above the EUR 12,500 threshold; no conversion ratio or liquidation obligation applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for EU/EEA-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (e.g., Lithuania- or Ireland-licensed EMIs) passported into Cyprus under PSD2; Low feasibility for offshore non-EU digital EMIs (UK, Singapore, Hong Kong) that lost EU passporting rights and would require separate CB Cyprus licensing or an EU-licensed agent. EMIs are permissible only as secondary settlement rails for marketplace receipts; the primary treasury banking relationship must remain with a CB Cyprus-licensed credit institution to satisfy Cypriot law, tax substance, and CBC KYC Directive requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory: CB Cyprus KYC directives require a face-to-face interview at a branch or with a delegated bank officer in Cyprus for at least two natural persons, typically a director and the ultimate beneficial owner. Remote video onboarding is available only for existing clients or where the company presents a credible external KYC introduction from an EU correspondent bank, a Big-4 auditor, or a Cypriot licensed legal firm; even then, apostilled notarized corporate documents and passport copies must accompany the remote verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner with an asset-light personal profile and cross-border source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO passport with apostille, tax residence certificate, three years of personal bank statements, sworn declaration of funds origin, source-of-wealth narrative supported by share sale agreements or family capital proof, and an introduction letter from a Cyprus-licensed attorney or Big-4 audit firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party clearing exposure arising from Amazon Pay and Stripe marketplace settlements creating perceived disguised payment masking
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amazon seller verification certificate, Stripe merchant agreement, 12-month settlement statements, underlying sales invoices and packing lists, Intrastat and customs export declarations (SAD/EXA), and the company's VAT registration certificate proving economic substance in the order-to-cash cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory license requirement for placing toys on the EU market under Directive 2009/48/EC (Toy Safety Directive) and national Cyprus product safety control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid CE certificate of conformity with EN 71-1/2/3 mechanical, flammability and chemical safety standards, EU Declaration of Conformity issued by the manufacturer, ISO 9001 quality management certificate, product liability insurance policy, and import authorization records from the Cyprus State General Laboratory or competent market surveillance authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume import of beechwood raw material from third countries, raising commodity-financing and sanctions-red-flag concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Timber supply contracts with incoterms, FSC or PEFC chain-of-custody certification substantiating the eco-friendly claim, bills of lading and CMR waybills, customs duty and VAT payment receipts, country-of-origin certificates, and a formal sanctions screening report for all counterparties from international screening databases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or sanctions-list hit on beneficial owners from jurisdictions presenting higher money-laundering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive World-Check / Dow Jones due diligence reports with resolutions, negative-news remediation memorandum, sworn affidavit confirming no sanctioned or Kremlin-linked affiliations, board resolution adopting a sanctions compliance policy, and independent legal opinion issued by a Cyprus-licensed counsel confirming the ownership chain is clean.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the UBO's personal or holding-company account to the company's EUR/USD capital escrow account. The MT103 field 70 (Remittance Information) must cite 'Equity subscription / Share capital contribution — [Entity Name] HE77, Cyprus'; the industry purpose code under the ECB BoP/IIP Manual should be entered as 'EQUI' (equity capital) or 'OCOR' (other capital income). Before operational use, the company must file the shareholder resolution, update the Cyprus Beneficial Ownership Register under the Cyprus Companies Law (Cap. 113), and report the transaction to the CB Cyprus if it equals or exceeds EUR 12,500. No exchange-control permit is required, but all remittance documents must be retained to demonstrate traceability of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The compliant clearing rails for outbound trade settlements are: (i) SWIFT MT103 international wires with field 70 citing the underlying commercial invoice number and purpose code 'GDSV' or 'THRU' for goods; (ii) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for euro payments to EU suppliers of packaging, glue, and finishing materials; (iii) commercial documentary letters of credit issued subject to UCP600 by Bank of Cyprus or Hellenic Bank, with the beneficiary bank in the supplier country as advising bank, for bulk beechwood shipments; (iv) trade finance facilities such as import loans or pre-export financing against purchase orders; and (v) automated repatriation of Amazon Pay and Stripe marketplace settlements into the operational account via devoted collection accounts. Any outgoing settlement exceeding EUR 12,500 must be supported by export/trade invoices and, where applicable, Intrastat or customs declaration numbers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards with tenors up to 12 months against Amazon Pay USD-denominated receivables
Deliverable EUR/GBP FX forwards for UK wholesale distribution collections
FX swaps and rollover swaps on EUR/USD to align mismatched settlement value dates
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) confined to non-deliverable Asian exotics (e.g., CNY, INR) solely to hedge raw-material import cost exposure
Vanilla EUR/USD currency options and zero-cost collars, subject to the bank's credit approval and the company's documented treasury risk policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (RCOR), Nicosia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the company's annual return date (anniversary of incorporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default penalty under Companies Law Cap.113; the company and each director/officer may be fined; late filing blocks Certificate of Good Standing and may trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (RCOR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty accrues in tranches (EUR 50 / 100 / 150 over successive three-month periods); continued non-payment leads to the company's removal from the Register and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (unless audit exemption applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (RCOR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 42 days after the annual return date, attached to or accompanied by the HE32 Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited statements is a criminal offence for the company and each officer; sanctions include monetary fines and administrative strike-off after persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: UBO Register, Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (RCOR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, not later than 30 June, aligned with the annual levy and annual return cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with UBO Law 13(I)/2021 subjects the company and each responsible officer to fines of up to EUR 20,000 and potential criminal sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Cypriot private limited company is compulsorily subject to statutory audit unless it qualifies as a 'small company' for two consecutive years by not exceeding two of the three thresholds: total assets EUR 350,000; net turnover EUR 700,000; average employees 10. Audit exemption is always denied to public/subsidiary/group undertakings and to companies required by EU Directives to publish audited accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the EU; qualifying small and micro companies may prepare their accounts using the IFRS for SMEs framework or simplified SME financial reporting provisions in line with the EU Accounting Directive.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered UBO list must be re-confirmed annually when making the HE32 Annual Return. Any transfer of shares or beneficial ownership affecting more than 25% of the company must be filed with the UBO Register within 30 days of the change. The annual confirmation records the natural persons (or, in exceptional cases, non-U.K. PSEs) who control the entity, and failure to confirm removes the duty holder's compliance shield.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 – 1,500 per annum for Cyprus registered office and licensed corporate services agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 – 3,000 per annum for a low-risk manufacturing SME

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat corporate income tax rate on the worldwide income of Cyprus tax-resident companies (Income Tax Law L.118(I)/2002, s.40).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box regime: 80% deduction of qualifying IP profits yields a 2.5% effective rate; Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on new equity capital at the 10-year Cyprus government bond yield plus 3 percentage points; participation exemption for dividend income; exemption from income tax on gains from disposal of securities; SME relief of 20% on qualifying new payroll and 7% on qualifying new tangible fixed assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form TD (Annual Company Income Tax Return), filed electronically through the TaxisNet portal of the Cyprus Tax Department (taxisnet.mof.gov.cy); audited financial statements must be attached.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax returns (Form TD6) are filed and paid in three instalments during the tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Form TD is due within 15 months after the end of the tax year (for a calendar-year company: 31 March of the second subsequent year). Provisional tax instalments are due on 31 July, 30 September and 31 December of the tax year; a newly incorporated company must submit its first provisional return within six months from the end of the month in which it commenced business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, Tax Identification Number (TIN), registration number and Cyprus registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Cypriot HE registration number; verify the entity remains managed and controlled in Cyprus; the foreign shareholder's details must not be shown as the Cyprus address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover and gross receipts from the sale of goods (Montessori wooden blocks and related toys).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide gross sales including Amazon Pay and Stripe settlement volumes; convert foreign-currency receipts at the Central Bank of Cyprus exchange rate; reconcile settlement fees as expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales: raw beechwood, pigments, packaging and direct manufacturing labor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use incurred-cost basis consistent with audited IFRS financial statements; VAT incurred is not deductible in the corporate income tax return; customs import costs are capitalized into inventory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit or gross loss after deducting cost of sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the gross margin on sales to any related foreign distributor is arm's length and supported by a benchmarking study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other income: interest, royalties, exchange gains, and miscellaneous income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest income from related-party loans is taxable and should be priced at arm's length; exchange gains are taxable unless covered by a specific exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, directors' remuneration and social insurance contributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only remuneration relating to actual services performed in or for the Cyprus entity is deductible; excessive fees to foreign directors without substance may be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rents, royalties, management fees and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border management fees and royalties paid to a foreign related party are deductible only at arm's length and subject to withholding tax where applicable; retain service evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General operating expenses: utilities, e-commerce platform fees, marketing, quality testing and CE conformity costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be wholly and exclusively incurred for the Cyprus company's business; related-party payments must satisfy the economic substance and arm's length standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital allowances (tax depreciation) on tangible fixed assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim annual capital allowances on production equipment at the statutory rates; rates depend on asset class and investment-zone designation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest payable on borrowings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to foreign related lenders is deductible subject to arm's length rate, thin capitalization and the EU/ATAD interest-limitation rules; excessive or unsubstantiated interest is added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile to the audited profit-and-loss account; non-deductible items (entertainment exceeding limits, fines, penalties) must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result before exemptions and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the pre-incentive accounting profit adjusted for tax add-backs and capital allowances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income: dividend income qualifying for the participation exemption and gains from disposal of securities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The participation exemption applies where the Cyprus company holds at least 1% of the payer's share capital or voting rights; documentary evidence of the holding period is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred in tax years 2015 and onward may be set off, and only within the five-year carryforward window.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Notional Interest Deduction on new equity capital introduced after 1 January 2015.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders injecting equity must document the injection date and amount; the deduction is capped at 80% of taxable profit before NID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IP Box deduction: 80% of qualifying profits from qualifying intangible assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applicable only if the company owns patented or functionally equivalent IP and undertakes qualifying R&D; the deduction requires full tracing of development costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after exemptions and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The amount subject to the 12.5% headline tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at 12.5%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the flat rate to Line 17; no lower band for small companies applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, Cypriot withholding credits, and any other creditable taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax on overseas income may be credited against Cyprus tax, capped at the Cyprus effective tax on the same income; attach proof of foreign tax payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of tax payable or refundable after provisional tax instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Set off the three provisional instalments; balancing payment is due by 31 March of the second subsequent year; late payment attracts interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Automatic late-filing penalty of EUR 100 plus EUR 100 per month or part of month of delay, up to a maximum of EUR 1,200; late-payment interest at 2.5% per annum; best-of-judgment tax assessment where no return is filed; additional administrative penalties up to 5% of the assessed tax and criminal fines up to EUR 5,000 and/or imprisonment up to three years for fraudulent returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0%: Cyprus does not impose dividend withholding tax on dividends paid by a Cyprus-resident company to non-resident shareholders. The former Special Defence Contribution on dividends and interest income was abolished with effect from 1 January 2024 and never applied to non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the statutory dividend withholding rate is 0%, treaty relief is generally not required at source for dividends. For interest and royalties, the Cyprus payer must obtain from the non-resident beneficiary: (i) a valid Cyprus Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction; (ii) a completed withholding tax relief application submitted to the Cyprus Tax Department (Form WHT/IR or equivalent); and (iii) a beneficial ownership and economic substance declaration. EU-connected corporate recipients may invoke the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (dividends) and the EU Interest & Royalties Directive (interest and royalties) where the 25% direct or indirect shareholding threshold and minimum holding period are met; Cyprus applies the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI before granting treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory withholding on payments for the use of patents, trademarks, designs, know-how, or industrial/commercial equipment; 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive where the EU-connected payer qualifies; most Cyprus double tax agreements provide rates of 0% to 10%. Interest: 0% domestic withholding on interest paid to non-residents unless the interest is attributable to a permanent establishment in Cyprus, in which case the PE income is taxed at the 12.5% corporate rate; treaty rates are typically 0% to 10%; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive grants 0% withholding for qualified intra-EU interest and royalty payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Where related-party financial transactions exceed EUR 5,000,000 and/or all other related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 in aggregate per tax year, the Cyprus entity must prepare a Local File and submit the electronic TP Documentation Summary (Form TPD) together with the annual tax return (Cyprus Tax Department Decree 533/2022). Master File obligations arise only at MNE group level where consolidated group revenue is at least EUR 750,000,000 under Country-by-Country Reporting rules.
